role_in_set: Companion umbrella subject to the animal cell, closing the organelles set: the generic textbook plant cell, rendered explicitly FOR CONTRAST with the animal cell next to it in the catalogue. Everything the animal cell has, plus the three plant additions - rigid cellulose cell wall, green chloroplasts, one huge central vacuole. Not a human cell and not one particular plant tissue; it is the plant blueprint.

morphology.summary: A generic plant cell: a RECTANGULAR/boxy polygonal outline with softly rounded corners, set by the rigid cellulose CELL WALL (primary wall over a thin middle lamella shared with neighbours), with the plasma membrane pressed just inside the wall. ONE LARGE CENTRAL VACUOLE - often more than 80% of the interior - bounded by its own single membrane (the tonoplast), filled with clear watery cell sap, pushes the cytoplasm into a thin peripheral strip against the wall. In that strip: the nucleus pressed to the periphery (double envelope with pores, heterochromatin, one nucleolus), several lens-shaped green CHLOROPLASTS each with a double envelope and internal thylakoid membranes stacked into grana (coin-stacks), smaller bean-shaped MITOCHONDRIA with wavy cristae (plant cells have BOTH chloroplasts and mitochondria), rough ER cisternae with ribosome dots near the nucleus, one small Golgi stack (dictyosome), free ribosome dots, and fine cytoskeleton threads. PLASMODESMATA cross the wall as thin cytoplasmic channels. The honest classic teaching view is a CUTAWAY/SECTIONED cell so the vacuole's dominance shows.
morphology.kind: generic plant cell (the shared blueprint of plant tissue cells); an umbrella/contrast subject, not a species or a particular tissue
morphology.size: Typical plant cells run 10-100 um; a leaf mesophyll/parenchyma teaching figure is ~40-70 um - larger than the ~20 um generic animal cell. For orientation inside it: central vacuole 50-80%+ of the volume, chloroplasts lens-shaped 3-10 um long (clearly LARGER than mitochondria), mitochondria 0.5-1 um wide and 1-4 um long, nucleus ~5-8 um, cell wall 0.1-1 um thick for a primary wall (drawn as a distinctly thick band - unlike the membrane's single thin line), plasma membrane ~5-10 nm (one thin line), plasmodesmata ~50 nm channels (drawn as thin threads through the wall).
morphology.shape: Boxy - a rounded-cornered rectangle/polygon, because the rigid cellulose wall sets the shape and neighbouring cells press flat faces against each other. This is THE contrast with the animal cell's soft irregular blob: the wall means plant cells cannot crawl or swallow, they stack like bricks. Not a perfect geometric rectangle (corners are rounded, walls slightly bowed by turgor), but unmistakably angular.
morphology.number_per_cell: One nucleus with one nucleolus; ONE central vacuole (a single dominant compartment, not several); several chloroplasts in view (real mesophyll cells hold tens to ~100); a few mitochondria (standing for hundreds); one Golgi stack in view (plant cells actually hold many dispersed dictyosomes); thousands of ribosome dots; several plasmodesmata threads through the wall.
morphology.arrangement: The wall is the outermost layer; the plasma membrane hugs its inner face. The central vacuole fills the middle. Everything living squeezes into the thin cytoplasm strip between tonoplast and membrane: nucleus to one side/corner, chloroplasts spaced along the strip like beads (in life they can reposition with light), mitochondria between them, ER + Golgi near the nucleus. Nothing floats inside the vacuole - its sap is optically clear.

distinguishing_conventions.chloroplast_vs_mitochondrion: THE science check for this subject. Chloroplast = GREEN, LARGER (3-10 um), lens/discus-shaped, double envelope, interior holds neat COIN-STACK grana (stacked thylakoid discs) connected by thin lamellae in pale stroma. Mitochondrion = smaller (1-4 um), bean-shaped, NOT green (dusty-rose interior per this set's legend), inner membrane folded as WIDE WAVY CRISTAE RIBBONS like a rippled curtain. Coin-stacks vs wavy curtains; green vs rose; big lens vs small bean.
distinguishing_conventions.wall_vs_membrane: Cell wall = a thick sand/straw-coloured band, the outermost layer, rigid and angular. Plasma membrane = ONE thin teal line pressed against the wall's inner face. Two different things, always both present, never merged.
distinguishing_conventions.vacuole: ONE huge central compartment bounded by ONE thin membrane line (the tonoplast), interior a pale watery translucent tint with nothing inside. Not many small bubbles, not a second nucleus, not grey cytosol.
distinguishing_conventions.nucleus: Same convention as the set's nucleus subject: double envelope (two close parallel blue lines) with amber pore rings, heterochromatin patches at the rim, one denser nucleolus with no membrane of its own - but pressed to the cell's periphery by the vacuole, never centred.
distinguishing_conventions.plasmodesmata: Thin cytoplasm threads crossing the full thickness of the wall, connecting to the neighbour side; drawn as a few subtle channels, not gaping holes.

do_not_draw: No CENTRIOLES - higher plant cells lack them (they organise spindles without centrioles). The animal cell has them; the plant cell must not.
No lysosomes as drawn bodies - the vacuole covers the lytic role in the plant teaching diagram.
No soft irregular blobby outline - the wall makes the outline angular, a rounded-cornered rectangle/polygon.
No crowd of small vacuoles - ONE dominant central vacuole.
No organelles floating INSIDE the vacuole - chloroplasts, nucleus and mitochondria live only in the thin peripheral cytoplasm strip.
No green mitochondria and no wavy-curtain interior in chloroplasts - grana coin-stacks belong to chloroplasts, wavy cristae to mitochondria, and mixing them is this subject's defining error.
No centred nucleus - the vacuole presses it to the periphery.

No baked-in text of ANY kind. Like the animal cell, this is one of the most label-contaminated diagrams in every textbook training set: practically every printed version carries lettered callouts. All surfaces must be clean, unlettered biological material; verification must check magnified crops of every region.
No metaphase (X-shaped) chromosomes in the intact nucleus.
No bacterial structures (flagellum, pili, capsule, nucleoid).
No membrane drawn around the nucleolus.
No anthropomorphising in the scientific plates (faces belong only on the colouring page).

colour_legend: Chloroplast green is the one REAL colour in this subject (chlorophyll); everything else keeps the set's teaching-convention legend. Cell wall warm sand/straw (#D9C79A) band with a slightly darker middle-lamella line; plasma membrane thin teal line; central vacuole very pale watery blue translucent fill; tonoplast a slightly deeper thin blue line; chloroplasts grass-green (#5B8C3E) lens bodies with darker green grana coin-stacks and paler stroma; nucleus per the set (outer #6B8CB8 / inner #4C6E9E envelope blues, amber #F2B441 pores, dusty-purple #7B4B8A heterochromatin, lavender euchromatin, terracotta #D9622B nucleolus); mitochondria steel-blue outer membrane with warm dusty-rose (#C98A7A) cristae interior; rough ER cool grey-blue (#9AA7B5) with dark slate ribosome dots; Golgi dusty sage-green (#8FAE8B) - greyer and duller than the chloroplasts' vivid grass green; cytosol warm translucent cream/tan strip; fine pale cytoskeleton threads.

No baked-in text or scale bar, so no cleaning needed beyond fetch_reference.py's deterministic square crop + upscale.
